title: Digital Inputs: Pushbuttons & Internal Pullups
summary: Sense physical button presses without phantom triggers! Learn the secret of INPUT_PULLUP and debouncing.

steps.title: Buttons and Open Circuits
steps.markdownContent: Robots need bump switches and limit sensors to detect physical collisions. A momentary tactile pushbutton is a mechanical bridge: when pressed, two internal metal contacts connect, completing a circuit path.

steps.title: The Floating Pin Trap
steps.markdownContent:
Microcontroller input pins have enormous internal resistance (>100 MΩ). If an input is not firmly connected to either 5V or GND, it **floats** like an open antenna, picking up 60Hz wall hum and electrostatic fields, causing random false triggers!

To prevent this, every digital input must be tied to a stable reference voltage using a pull-up or pull-down resistor.

steps.title: Pushbutton Breadboard Placement
steps.markdownContent:
Wire a tactile pushbutton using active-low logic:
1. Place the 4-pin button so it straddles the center divider trench of your breadboard.
2. Connect one terminal to Uno Digital Pin `2`.
3. Connect the opposite terminal to Uno `GND`.
4. *Notice: No 5V wire or external resistor is needed on the breadboard!*
